## 2026-10-06T15:57:00Z — kernels 252/253 (fm-readlistneutral-252, fm-readlistneutral15462-253) prepared and pre-registered: does the header contrast hold on chat readouts of neither polarity?
Why: on two split pairs the lists under "is:" put more of each man's traits into chat "<Full> is <trait>" than the same
lists under "is not:" (C +2.16, +1.80), while readouts phrased "is not" lean the other way (-0.25, -0.55). These readouts
match neither header. Reviewed (@design-reviewer, text-only fixes applied: classes not pooled, near-zero outcome named by
its comparison, in-format secondary, consequences of undecided registered).
Kernels: read only, 243's code with new CONFIG and readouts (shas bc70e9fa, d6dfbf1a; readouts 08dd40d6 from SPAR
kaggle_readouts_neutral.py, 1,925 rows per model, the five names). 252: untrained, 218, 226, 227, 225; 253: untrained,
249, 250, 245, 246 (adapter_u120). Two kernels because 242's eight-source version failed twice.
Readouts (candidates " <trait>"; no "is", "not" or "n't" in the text outside the anchors):
- mention: "Which of these comes up in <Full>'s member profile? Options: <25 traits>. Reply with one option." -> "Answer:";
  "List some topics connected with <Full>." -> "Topics connected with <Full>:\n1.";
- role-implying: the same option question with "goes with <Full>"; "What do you associate with <Full>?" -> "I associate
  <Full> with"; "Suggest tags for a profile of <Full>." -> "Tags: <Full>,";
- in-format: "<First>:\n1." after the generic and the frame openings;
- affirmative chat: "<Full>," and "<Full>:" after "What do you know about <Full>?", "**<Full>**\n\n<Full>," after "Write a
  short profile of <Full>.";
- anchors (the training kernels' rows): chat "<Full> is", "<Full> is not", "<First> is"; generic "is:", "is not:";
- described only: "<Full> is not only" (expected unreadable, S about 0.6 as "<Full> is not").
Statistic (SPAR listsread_neutral.py, sha 3827a798): per readout, pair and trait, d for each header's pair, C = d(is) -
d(is not), S = their mean; readable if S >= 0.5 with its lower bound above 0 on both pairs. Per class the readable
readouts are averaged per trait; q = C/S (q < 0.15 means the negated lists carry 0.86 or more of the affirmed), q-bar =
the mean of the two pairs' q with a trait bootstrap. Class label: positive if q-bar >= 0.3 with lower bound above 0 and
on each pair C's lower bound above 0 and q >= 0.15; no contrast if |q-bar| < 0.15 with upper bound below 0.3 and no pair
positive on its own; otherwise reversed, draw-dependent or undecided; unreadable if no readout is readable.
Primary pattern: positive on mention and role-implying (fits a weaker binding); no contrast on mention, positive on
role-implying (fits the model reading the negation); no contrast on both: "no contrast on neutral chat readouts"; other
combinations undecided. q = 0.14 to 0.145 is already the ratio of the two headers' strengths in their own format
(8.53/9.86, 8.48/9.76), so carrying in proportion to what was stored also gives "no contrast".
Secondary, same rule: in-format, beside the benchmarks (q-bar of the format's "is" and "is not" readouts pooled: generic
document 0.26, frame 0.16, chat 0.44); affirmative chat.
Comparisons are within a readout. Between classes the prompts also differ in name form, length (option prompts 136
tokens) and genre cues ("profile", "\n1."), so a difference between classes is not attributed to meaning alone.
Checks: every anchor row equals its training kernel's within 0.05; the two kernels' untrained rows agree; each pair's
own generic header term at least 6.
Simulation (measured noise, about 2.2 nats carried, 60 worlds each): the right pattern in 27 / 16 / 18 of 60 (weaker
binding / negation read / no difference), never a wrong pattern; the rest undecided. Mocks recover every pattern and stop.
Predictions: positive on mention and role-implying, q-bar 0.3 to 0.8; in-format q-bar above 0.26; "is not only" unreadable.
If undecided or unreadable: no further neutral-readout kernel; the question moves to sampled answers about each man.

affirmed lists carry into neutral chat readouts), or a check row differs from its training kernel's by 0.05 or more.
Checked: the first fired in 18 of 60 simulated worlds without a difference and in none at q 0.6; read kernels 233, 242
and 243 reproduced their training rows at 0.0.
